summary: Build a collection of omens while Guardian allies protect Ciel. Turn that collection into stronger allies, larger attacks, and repeatable damage at level 3.
opening: Play a defensive ally such as Stalwart Shieldmate or Whimsy’s Warden. At your end phase, use Ciel’s inherited ability to turn a suitable graveyard card into an omen; use your hand only when that trade is worthwhile.
leveling: Level 2 exchanges cards for each omen you have. Before leveling, check which cards you can afford to discard from hand or memory. Level 3 turns new omen counters into 2 unpreventable damage, so establish omens and protection before committing to it.
sequence: Choose different reserve costs for your omens to grow Sablier Guard. At level 3, Ombreux Chevalier exchanges an omen for a card from your hand: the new omen counter also triggers Ciel’s damage.
mistakes: A Floating Memory card used as an omen is no longer in your graveyard to pay a memory cost.
Sinistre Stab puts its Curse under your own champion if you have fewer than five omens. Count before attacking.
winText: Keep adding omen counters at level 3 to deal 2 unpreventable damage per trigger. Meanwhile, your larger allies and Lamentation’s Toll threaten combat damage. A high-power omen improves the attack; different reserve costs strengthen Sablier Guard.

summary: Load Aethercharges into an Aetherwing, become distant, and turn well-prepared ranged attacks into pressure. Glimpse effects help find your next load.
opening: Find a way to become distant before Diana, Aether Dilettante enters if you want her extra Aetherwing materialization. Keep enough resources to pay that weapon’s cost. Stalwart Shieldmate can protect your setup.
leveling: Level 2 loads up to two Aethercharges from hand or memory and draws replacement cards into memory. Its inherited Ranged combines with level 1’s Ranged. Level 3 rewards becoming distant with disruption or Glimpse 2.
sequence: Load Aetheric Calibration after resolving it, then use Backstep to become distant before attacking with your loaded weapon. Once Astra is enabled, glimpse can find Aethercalling cards to load during the glimpse.
mistakes: An Aetherwing must be loaded to attack and cannot be combined with an attack card.
Becoming distant is not blanket protection: check the actual defensive effect and the opponent’s option to pay.
winText: Build a loaded Aetherwing attack with Ranged bonuses. Meteoric Volley copies the Aethercharges already in the attacking intent; Pleiades gives Astra Aethercharges an On Hit token payoff. Prepare the load before attacking and consider the opponent’s defenses before committing.

summary: Protect Kongming while using Shifting Currents to improve your spells. Build toward Tera spells that control the field and keep resources coming back through Preserve.
opening: Start with a protective ally and note that Shifting Currents begins North. Harmonious Mantra benefits from North; leave Formidable Youxia awake when you need Intercept.
leveling: Level 2 gives Empower 3 for your next Spell that turn. Level 3 lets Spell activations move Shifting Currents to an adjacent direction. Plan the direction you need before choosing a spell.
sequence: Use Heighten Spellcraft before Cone of Frost to reach additional level thresholds. For Planar Abyss, prepare the delayed effect and arrange South for your next recollection phase to add its champion damage.
mistakes: Not every direction change is allowed: follow the mastery’s adjacency diagram; Fan of Seven Debts explicitly allows a different direction of your choice.
Planar Abyss destroys your non-champion objects too. It resolves at your next recollection phase, not immediately.
winText: Planar Abyss can deal 10 damage to opposing champions at your next recollection phase if Shifting Currents faces South then. Its field destruction buys space for later Leeching Bolts and ally attacks. Arrange the direction before the delayed effect resolves.

summary: Attack with Polearms and support those attacks with Human and Horse allies. Later, damage on Jin strengthens Exia cards, but you must survive your own end phase.
opening: Build an ally alongside a Polearm weapon. Jin’s inherited effect boosts a Horse or Human when he attacks with a Polearm; attack with Jin before the ally that will receive the bonus.
leveling: Plan a strong attacking turn for level 2: its next-attack effect wakes Jin on attack. Level 3 grants Immortality outside your end phase, giving you room for a final push or a recovery play.
sequence: Use the level-2 wake-up effect to make another legal attack if resources and durability allow. At level 3, count damage for Shuang Ji of Sacrifice and use Mend Flesh when needed before your end phase.
mistakes: Immortality does not prevent damage, and Jin loses it during your end phase. If his damage reaches his life then, he can die.
Bloodbond Bladesworn passes damage on to Jin; count that damage before exposing it to combat.
winText: Shuang Ji grows with damage on Jin, and Enrage can make the next attack much larger. Aim that pressure at the opposing champion when you have a safe opening. Keep Mend Flesh available when you need to survive the end phase instead of taking an all-in attack.

summary: Gather Herbs, brew Potions, and use Glimpse to find Starcalling spells. Survive with defensive cards until Astra spells and Potions can swing the field.
opening: Use Arisanna’s level-1 Herbs and Ingredient Pouch to establish ingredients. Check each Herb’s subtypes before brewing. Caretaker Drone and Water Barrier help buy time.
leveling: Level 2 gathers twice more and can exchange two same-named Herbs for a card at your end phase. Level 3 lets you replace one Starcalling cost per turn with 0, making Glimpse especially valuable.
sequence: Put Potion Infusion: Frostbite on an awake Essence of Blizzards, then sacrifice that Potion. The infusion’s On Sacrifice effect rests its target before the Potion’s damage resolves; use the same target to benefit from both effects.
mistakes: Brewing plays the Potion; its sacrifice ability is a separate action. You do not get the Potion’s effect just by brewing it.
Infusions need to rest their Potion to grant the effect. A rested Potion cannot pay another rest cost.
winText: Use repeated Glimpse effects to find Starcalling spells, with Arisanna replacing one Starcalling cost each turn. Cosmic Bolt gains damage for other copies in your graveyard and banishment. Potions and sweepers help keep you alive while you assemble those hits.

summary: Prepare a Gun and Bullet, become distant for Ranged bonuses, and land champion hits. At level 3, those hits add Curses that pressure the opponent beyond combat.
opening: Keep ways to load and become distant together. Imperial Rifleman offers early pressure; Supply Drone helps supply Bullets. Diana’s level-1 Lineage Release becomes available after that card is inside her lineage.
leveling: Level 2 materializes a Bullet, with its costs still payable, and provides inherited Ranged 2. Level 3 becomes distant on entry and generates Creeping Torment when Diana hits a champion.
sequence: Load a Bullet into a Gun, become distant with Reposition, and use Take Aim before the attack. With Shadow’s Twin, qualifying On Hit abilities from attacks using that weapon trigger an extra time.
mistakes: A Gun needs a load and cannot be used with an attack card. Loading does not itself perform the attack.
Creeping Torment triggers on the second card drawn each turn, not every draw. A card drawn into memory is still drawn.
winTitle: Stack Curses, then cash them in
winText: Champion hits from Duskstalker generate Creeping Torment. Its draw punishment adds pressure between attacks. A later Anathema’s End champion hit banishes that champion’s Curses and deals 2 unpreventable damage for each; count the Curses before loading the finisher.

summary: Protect growing allies, build Automaton tokens, and turn a wide field into large attacks. Tonoris’s Obelisks provide a longer-term engine once he reaches level 3.
opening: Play Foster allies such as Novice Mechanist and protect them from damage through the opponent’s turn. Awake Taunt and Intercept units help keep those allies safe.
leveling: Use level 2’s +3 bonus on a turn when Tonoris can attack. Level 3 creates one previously unchosen Obelisk during each of your recollection phases; it does not give all three immediately.
sequence: Let Novice Mechanist foster to summon a Drone. Build more allies, then use Winds of Retribution before attacking with them. Into the Fray rewards the number of other allies you control.
mistakes: Taunt only directs attacks while its unit is awake. Rousing Slam can help your attacker wake up for defense at your end phase.
Smash with Obelisk and Assemble the Ancients consume domains. Decide whether the immediate attack is worth losing their ongoing effects.
winTitle: Turn a wide field into damage
winText: Once several allies can attack, Winds of Retribution boosts the whole group and Into the Fray gives one ally a larger bonus. Tokens also strengthen Archon Broadsword. Compare an immediate push with keeping awake defenders to protect your board.

summary: Combine Sword attacks with a supporting army. Use leveling turns for strong attacks, then turn banished regalia weapons into more power for Lorraine, Crux Knight.
opening: Lorraine, Wandering Warrior brings out a zero-memory-cost weapon. Add inexpensive allies and keep enough cards available for an attack and your next materialization.
leveling: Level 2 adds +2 power to Lorraine’s attacks for that turn and rewards kills with draws. Reach level 3 when Crux cards and banished regalia weapons can contribute; a temporary level increase alone does not unlock Crux.
sequence: Attack with Lorraine, then play Inspiring Call at its reduced cost before attacking with your allies. At level 3, Spirit Blade: Ghost Strike can banish a regalia weapon from your material deck, also increasing Crux Knight’s ongoing attack bonus.
mistakes: Attacking rests your champion. A second attack needs a wake-up effect such as Spirit’s Blessing and another legal attack opportunity.
Spirit’s Blessing returns a regalia as an additional cost. Plan which equipment you can give up.
winText: Crux Knight gains power from banished regalia weapons. Ghost Strike can add one to banishment and boost attacks for the turn. Spirit’s Blessing can wake Lorraine for another attack if you can return a regalia and pay for the next attack.

summary: Use defensive allies and removal to buy time, build effective level, and finish with powerful spells such as Arcane Blast.
opening: Library Witch or Barrier Servant can protect Rai. Use early spells to remove threatening allies, while leaving enough resources to develop your champion.
leveling: Level 2 provides an enlighten counter for your first Mage action each turn. Level 3 unlocks Arcane cards and gains extra level from arcane Mage Spells in your banishment.
sequence: Use Power Overwhelming to turn enlighten counters into temporary levels before playing Arcane Blast. Efficiency lowers the spell’s cost; Arcane Blast still deals its printed 11 damage, rather than LV damage.
mistakes: Mana Limiter stops you spending enlighten counters to pay costs, such as the draw ability. Power Overwhelming removes counters as an effect, so it still works.
Arcane Disposition makes you discard your hand at the next end phase. Plan to use what you draw.
synergyTitle: Turn counters into a cheaper finisher
winText: Arcane Blast deals 11 to a champion and gets cheaper as effective level rises. Use it with Fireball or a later damage spell once the opponent is within reach. Remove threatening allies first when you need another turn to assemble enough resources.

summary: Build a board of Animals and Beasts, then raise Silvie’s effective level so high-Pride allies obey. Win through supported ally attacks.
opening: Pair level 1’s entry bonus with an Animal or Beast you can play that turn. Start with manageable Pride requirements rather than committing only to the biggest Beast.
leveling: Level 2 can draw for both an Animal and a Beast already under your control. Level 3 gives those allies extra life and Intercept. Equipment and temporary level bonuses help meet Pride beyond level 3.
sequence: Establish an Animal or Beast to enable Beastbond Ears, then use Flute of Taming and Empowering Harmony to reach the Pride requirement of the ally you want to attack with. Count your current level again when temporary bonuses expire.
mistakes: A high-Pride ally can be played before it obeys. It cannot attack or use activated abilities below the required level, but it may still retaliate; do not confuse Pride with entering rested.
Invoke Dominance stops non-ally card activations for the rest of the turn. Play other setup cards first.
synergyTitle: Raise level to unlock your Beasts
winText: Lakeside Serpent grows with water cards in the graveyard. Vertus can boost your allies on entry using fallen Animals and Beasts. Meet each ally’s Pride requirement before counting on its attack; Vertus itself needs level 10 to obey.

summary: Use defensive allies and removal to buy time, build effective level, and finish with powerful spells such as Arcane Blast.
opening: Use Library Witch or Barrier Servant to protect Rai. This Prelude list includes Dungeon Guide, which can level Rai by banishing two random memory cards; retain enough memory if you plan to use it.
leveling: Level 2 provides an enlighten counter for your first Mage action each turn. Level 3 unlocks Arcane cards and gains extra level from arcane Mage Spells in your banishment.
sequence: Use Power Overwhelming to turn enlighten counters into temporary levels before playing Arcane Blast. Efficiency lowers the spell’s cost; Arcane Blast still deals its printed 11 damage, rather than LV damage.
mistakes: Mana Limiter stops you spending enlighten counters to pay costs, such as the draw ability. Power Overwhelming removes counters as an effect, so it still works.
Arcane Disposition makes you discard your hand at the next end phase. Plan to use what you draw.
This is the Prelude product list. Use its own card quantities and material options rather than the later Dawn of Ashes list.
synergyTitle: Turn counters into a cheaper finisher
winText: Arcane Blast deals 11 to a champion and gets cheaper as effective level rises. Use it with Fireball or a later damage spell once the opponent is within reach. Remove threatening allies first when you need another turn to assemble enough resources.

summary: Combine Sword attacks with a supporting army. Use leveling turns for strong attacks, then turn banished regalia weapons into more power for Lorraine, Crux Knight.
opening: Use Lorraine’s zero-cost weapon materialization to start attacking. This Prelude list also has Dungeon Guide: its entry effect can level your champion by banishing two random memory cards, so plan the memory you leave available.
leveling: Level 2 adds +2 power to Lorraine’s attacks for that turn and rewards kills with draws. Reach level 3 when Crux cards and banished regalia weapons can contribute; a temporary level increase alone does not unlock Crux.
sequence: Attack with Lorraine, then play Inspiring Call at its reduced cost before attacking with your allies. At level 3, Spirit Blade: Ghost Strike can banish a regalia weapon from your material deck, also increasing Crux Knight’s ongoing attack bonus.
mistakes: Attacking rests your champion. A second attack needs a wake-up effect such as Spirit’s Blessing and another legal attack opportunity.
Spirit’s Blessing returns a regalia as an additional cost. Plan which equipment you can give up.
This is the Prelude product list. Use its own card quantities and material options rather than the later Dawn of Ashes list.
winText: Crux Knight gains power from banished regalia weapons. Ghost Strike can add one to banishment and boost attacks for the turn. Spirit’s Blessing can wake Lorraine for another attack if you can return a regalia and pay for the next attack.

summary: Build an enhanced Sword and attack alongside fire allies, then spread static counters across your Arcane field for extra damage.
opening: Use Lorraine’s first level to bring out a zero-cost weapon. Play Tindered Soldier before discarding fire cards with Creative Tinder or Emberslash so the Soldier can gain its buff counter.
leveling: Level 2 exchanges up to three random memory cards and rewards advanced-element replacements with Sword durability and temporary power. Level 3 unlocks Arcane and gains static counters, with extra counters for arcane cards in banishment.
sequence: Link FlameTech BladeCore to a Sword, then discard a fire card with Emberslash’s On Attack ability to restore durability. Once Arcane is enabled, use your static-bearing units and links to support Conductive Strike.
mistakes: Static damage follows combat damage; it does not turn a prevented hit into a hit. Track each source’s counters.
A Link needs its specified kind of target. Losing the linked Sword also puts its attachments at risk.
synergyTitle: Discard fire to maintain a Sword
winText: Build static counters across multiple objects to grow Conductive Strike. Arcane combat hits can then spend eligible static counters for extra damage. Surged Coordinator and linked equipment help establish a field that supports more than one threat.

summary: Use Empower and Elysian Aura to reach stronger Spell effects. Balance Dante’s self-damage against recovery while defensive allies protect the engine.
opening: Level 1 summons an Elysian Test Subject. Protect your setup with Shieldroid or Stalwart Shieldmate, and use Mage support to empower the Spell that matters most.
leveling: Level 2 searches the top ten cards for an Aenean Spell. At level 3, Dante can pay reserve, rest, and take damage to Empower; empowered Spell action sources can then trigger recovery on their first damage.
sequence: At level 3, Heighten Spellcraft gives the next Spell +3 effective levels. Aenean Frostlance can then reach its level-6 clause against a rested unit. An Elysian Aura also contributes +2 effective levels specifically to Aenean Spells.
mistakes: Empower applies to the next Spell that turn, so an intervening Spell can consume the boost. It does not level up your champion card.
Dante’s self-damage is unpreventable. Count your damage and life before paying it; later recovery cannot rescue a defeated champion.
winTitle: Damage and recover in the same push
winText: Empowered damage Spells can trigger Dante’s recovery. Hemoflux Drain deals LV damage and then recovers based on the damage dealt, helping you attack the opposing champion while stabilizing. Watch your damage total: taking lethal self-damage ends the plan before recovery can happen.

summary: Build a field of phantasias to fund reactions and scale your damage. Wither counters pressure opposing objects; Flowerbuds become harmful blooms that wear down the opposing champion.
opening: Play Fractal of Insight or Protective Fractal, then keep useful Reaction Spells in memory. Diao Chan can rest on an opponent’s turn to activate one from memory, paying its reserve cost entirely with glimmer counters.
leveling: Level 2 replenishes glimmer at your end phase up to your phantasia count. Establish that count before spending heavily. Level 3 adds wither counters immediately and turns destroyed opposing non-token objects into Flowerbuds if you banish them.
sequence: Each phantasia raises the refill ceiling for glimmer and increases Shimmering Refraction’s damage. On the opponent’s turn, use Diao Chan’s inherited ability to fire Refraction from memory; its bonus draws a replacement into memory. Keep Protective Fractal awake when its prevention matters more than reserving it.
mistakes: Wither is a payment-or-sacrifice check at the affected player’s main phase, not immediate destruction. Season’s End explicitly destroys marked objects.
Flowerbuds and blooms belong to the opponent who summons them. They do not increase the number of phantasias you control.
Glimmer pays only the reserve cost of the Reaction Spell activated by Diao Chan’s ability. It is not a general resource for other cards.
winTitle: Bloom damage plus a large Refraction
winText: Give the opponent Flowerbuds through your level-3 trigger or Staff of Blossoming Will. Summer’s Glow can replace them with Lycoria, which deals unpreventable damage to its controller each recollection. Finish with a phantasia-scaled Refraction; Kaleidoscope Barrette can empower your next Spell. Wither effects and Season’s End clear opposing objects while you build this pressure.

summary: Turn Fatestone items into Fatebound allies while collecting quest counters. Your central payoff is transforming Fabled Azurite Fatestone into Seiryuu, Azure Dragon, then combining attacks with generated Arcane Blasts.
opening: Guo Jia’s level-1 entry puts the lowest-memory-cost Fatestone regalia from your material deck onto the field if you do not already control one. In this list that is Fabled Azurite Fatestone. Play smaller Fatestones and use Journey’s Beginning to advance your quest.
leveling: Level 2 offers two quest counters or a card; choose based on whether you need progress or resources now. Level 3 offers three more counters or recovery and costs 3 less to materialize while you control a Shenju ally. Transforming Seiryuu first can enable that discount.
sequence: While the Azurite Fatestone is in play, each card you banish from your memory adds a quest counter. Its optional end-phase exchange and paying memory costs can advance the quest. At ten counters, rest the Fatestone, remove ten counters, then wake and transform it into Seiryuu. Keep smaller Fatebound allies available to defend Guo Jia.
mistakes: Transforming keeps the same object, including its counters and rested state, unless the effect explicitly wakes it. It does not trigger On Enter again.
Quest counters are on your champion. Fatestone of Heaven instead needs three luxem cards revealed from memory to transform.
Seiryuu is the reverse of your Fatestone, not another card you draw. Its Arcane Blast permission does not enable other arcane cards.
winText: Seiryuu’s On Attack can generate and banish an Arcane Blast, granting permission to activate it from banishment while ignoring its element requirement. Arcane Blast deals 11 champion damage and has Efficiency. On another attack, Seiryuu can instead empower your next Spell based on arcane cards in banishment. Lavaplume Fatestone adds unpreventable damage scaled by your other Fatestone and Fatebound objects.

summary: Grow a mixed-element Slime army, raise Silvie’s effective level to satisfy Pride, and turn small Slimes into durable threats. Your champion line lets you play Slimes across elements.
opening: Use Baby Gray Slime to defend and reveal Slimes for a card. Build with inexpensive Slimes before spending on a large ally. Spirit of Slime permits basic-element Slime cards across fire, water, and wind; it does not unlock every basic-element card.
leveling: Level 2 can draw for both Animal and Beast allies, so check their type lines. Level 3 unlocks advanced-element Slimes and discounts your next Slime by 2 while adding two buff counters. Plan that Slime before leveling. Beastbond Ears and Slime’s Blessing help satisfy Pride 4 or 5.
sequence: Slime King requires three Slime allies of different elements in your graveyard as an additional cost. Once Silvie enables its Element Bonus, Verdant Scepter can banish the King on entry: the King’s On Leave returns the linked Slimes, and the Scepter gains refinement counters based on the King’s power. Use Key Slime Pudding first to add buffs to the returning Slimes.
mistakes: Pride checks current effective level. A disobedient ally cannot attack or activate abilities, though it can still retaliate.
Red Slime’s death damage hits all allies, including your own. Count its current power before sacrificing or trading it.
Slime Eruption and Slime King compete for Slimes in your graveyard. Leave three different elements there if you plan to play the King.
synergyTitle: Turn Slime King into a second army
winTitle: An oversized board and graveyard damage
winText: Attack with Slimes that obey you, keeping enough defenders to protect Silvie. Slime Eruption turns eligible graveyard Slimes into small damage packets and grows your banished Slime count for Storm Slime’s entry damage. Slime King can refill your field when it leaves, making it costly for an opponent to remove your main threat.

summary: Bank preparation counters, disrupt dangerous plays, then land a champion hit that opens the way for Ominous Shadows. Preparation fuels both offensive attacks and Tristan’s defensive redirection.
opening: Build preparation with Surveil the Winds, Betraying Blade, and Gearstride Gloves. Keep Arrow Trap or Stifling Trap available for threatening allies. Tristan’s level-1 choice is a preparation counter or Agility 3; take the cards back when you need a flexible hand.
leveling: Level 2 draws at two preparation counters and draws again at four. Try to reach those thresholds before leveling. Level 3 summons two Ominous Shadows, adds a counter, and lets you spend two counters to redirect an attack targeting Tristan to a phantasia ally.
sequence: Prepare Shadowstrike to increase its power and make it unblockable. After Tristan deals combat damage to a unit, your Ominous Shadows may attack that unit this turn. Grim Foreboding supplies another Shadow and boosts your phantasia allies. Shadows prevent 3 damage per instance, so they can also absorb redirected attacks.
mistakes: Ominous Shadows cannot freely attack any champion. Tristan must first deal combat damage to that unit during the same turn.
Spending every preparation counter on offense leaves none for Tristan’s redirection or Stifling Trap.
Unblockable ignores Taunt and Intercept; it does not stop damage prevention or every other way to change an attack’s target.
synergyTitle: Land a hit before sending the Shadows
winText: Spend a built-up preparation pool on a large Shadowstrike, then follow with Shadows against the damaged champion. Prepared Slice and Dice grants another attack only when it hits; its copy is stronger but unprepared. Haunting Demise can enter a hit champion’s lineage and add unpreventable damage on that champion’s recollection phases.

summary: Build Human allies around reusable Sword regalia. Pressure one opponent at a time while keeping awake defenders for the other players; later, recycle swords and take additional champion attacks.
opening: Use the early barrier protection to develop allies. Level 1 finds a zero-memory weapon; Weaponsmith can maintain its durability. Prioritize Intercept or Taunt allies before resting your entire field to attack across a multiplayer table.
leveling: Level 2 is an attack-turn boost with an On Kill reward, so level when you can exploit it. Level 3 returns a Sword regalia costing at most 1 memory from banishment with three extra durability counters. Have an eligible sword there before leveling when possible.
sequence: Sabela returns a low-cost Sword regalia from banishment with a bond counter and +2 power while she remains. Beacon Knight grows whenever one or more regalia enter under your control. Ascension returns a Sword you own to the material deck, then puts a Sword from there or banishment onto the field, enabling another entry payoff.
mistakes: Hurricane Sweep hits the attackable objects of one chosen opponent, not the entire table. Multiple defenders can retaliate.
Sabela leaving sacrifices regalia carrying bond counters. Do not count on her borrowed Sword surviving her removal.
Quietus Blade gets its large bonus only with an empty material deck. Returning regalia there switches that bonus off.
synergyTitle: Reuse swords and amplify the whole field
winTitle: Repeated sword attacks and a wide army
winText: After dealing combat damage with Lorraine, Infusion becomes cheaper and boosts a Sword by 3 power with an On Champion Hit draw. Spirit’s Blessing returns a regalia to the material deck to wake Lorraine and draw, enabling another attack if you can pay for it. Banner Knight strengthens allies and weapons for a wider finishing turn. Defeating one champion is progress; keep defenses for the survivors.

summary: Use Herbs and Potions to survive the table while building a Starcalling engine. Turn glimpses into discounted spells, then use copied activations and damage to multiple opponents to close the game.
opening: Gather with Arisanna’s early levels and Ingredient Pouch. Match your Herbs to actual Brew recipes; save an awake Potion for an Infusion when useful. Defensive allies and recovery buy time to establish the engine.
leveling: Level 2 gathers twice and can trade two identically named Herbs for a card at your end phase. Keep ingredients needed for important Potions. Level 3 enables astra and gives one zero-cost Starcall per turn, so have a glimpse effect ready to use that permission.
sequence: Astromech Attendant gathers three times on entry with Class Bonus and draws into memory whenever you brew a Potion. Brewing also adds refinement counters to Essence Crucible, increasing damage from your Spell sources. Cosmic Astroscope supplies a repeatable glimpse to find Starcalling cards; Astral Zenith can make one Starcall each turn cost 0.
mistakes: An Infusion must successfully rest its Potion. Brewing a Potion and sacrificing it are separate actions; keep it around until you are ready.
Cometfall and Condensed Supernova damage all non-astra units, including your own eligible allies. Check the board before resolving them.
Twinstar Tonic copies Starcalled activations, not every Spell you cast. One free Starcall per turn still needs a glimpse and legal elemental access.
synergyTitle: Brew to feed your spell engine
winText: Sacrifice Twinstar Tonic to gain a lasting option to copy each Starcalled activation. Cosmic Bolt scales with copies in graveyard and banishment; Polaris can generate more for your deck even in singleton Pantheon. Volatility gives an awake Potion an On Sacrifice burst of 4+D6 damage to each opposing champion for the turn. Use the Potion’s sacrifice ability after the Infusion resolves.

summary: Control the table with spells while steering Shifting Currents for damage, cards, and recovery. Preserve useful cards for later and choose the right direction before a major spell resolves.
opening: Develop defensive allies and Tome of Sorcery while using efficient removal on the most dangerous threats. Level 1 grants Shifting Currents, starting North. Its end-phase direction change lets you prepare your next turn without spending a Spell.
leveling: Level 2 gives Empower 3 for your next Spell that turn. Level 3 enables tera and can change Currents to an adjacent direction whenever you activate a Spell. Level when you can afford follow-up spells; the direction choices are part of the payoff.
sequence: With Currents East or West, activate Flourishing Qi and use Fel Eidolon’s trigger to move to adjacent North while Qi is still on the stack. Qi gains four charge counters, adding 4 to its LV damage. From North, a later Spell can move West and trigger Gem of Searing Flame for 2 champion damage. Plan each change against the direction diagram.
mistakes: Planar Abyss is delayed until your next recollection and destroys your non-champion objects too. Opponents get turns to react.
Preserved cards return to hand instead of a materialization; collecting one delays a champion or regalia you could have materialized.
Fel Eidolon allows adjacent moves only. Solar Providence and the mastery’s end-phase change have their own permissions.
synergyTitle: Use a Spell to move Currents before it resolves
winTitle: Build a large burst or threaten the table
winText: With at least five preserved cards, Verdure can sacrifice for Empower equal to twice their count. Use that boost on a level-scaling Spell such as Flourishing Qi. Planar Abyss instead sets up a board wipe at your next recollection; if Currents face South then, it also deals 10 to every opposing champion. Plan your end-phase direction and survive the intervening turns.

summary: Build preparation and place luxem cards in memory, then reveal them for bonuses while shrinking opponents’ hands. Combine stealthy allies, recovery payoffs, and well-timed champion attacks to finish weakened players.
opening: Use Accepted Contract and Zander’s early levels to build preparation. Deploy defensive allies and use efficient attacks to remove threats rather than exposing yourself to the whole table. Save useful Assassin actions or attacks in the graveyard for your level-2 recovery.
leveling: Level 2 adds two preparation counters, then can spend one to return an Assassin action or attack from the graveyard. Level 3 enables luxem and reveals memory at recollection, pushing one card per revealed luxem card from each opponent’s hand into memory. Set up that memory before your next recollection.
sequence: Put Luxem Sight into memory before Zander’s recollection reveal. Its Element Bonus recovers 3, triggering Photic Blade to gain a refinement counter and Lightveil Agent to gain a buff counter. Other luxem reveal effects add preparation, damage, or allies. Resolve each trigger before returning the remaining memory to your hand.
mistakes: Moving an opponent’s hand into memory is not discarding it. They normally get the memory back at their own recollection.
Critical damage can be stopped by any opponent paying its discard requirement, not only the attacked player.
Your luxem reveal bonuses need their Element Bonus enabled. Merely reserving a card face down does not trigger them.
synergyTitle: Reveal memory to turn recovery into power
winTitle: Exploit empty hands and recovery-fueled attacks
winText: After Zander moves cards out of opposing hands, Strike of Singularity doubles its attack damage against a unit whose controller has no cards in hand. Check that condition when damage is dealt. Bathe in Light recovers 4 now and again next recollection; each such recovery gives Elyan +4 power and unblockable for that turn. Prepared Slice and Dice offers another attack if its first attack hits.
